comments.author: enneff
comments.why: Footage of id's SMB3 port that led to Keen
comments.text: They actually did a port of SMB3 and presented that to Nintendo. When Nintendo didn’t bite, they made new assets to make what became Keen. Here’s a video of the port: [VIDEO]

comments.author: ohithereyou
comments.story: Developers don’t want to show gameplay at E3 anymore
comments.why: id's SMB3 PC demo pitched to Nintendo
comments.text: One of the things that I wish was available to customers on a regular basis is the playable demo that was pitched to a company for a game that gets picked up. An example of this would be id software's demo for Super Mario Bros 3 on the PC[0] (even though that didn't get picked up). [0] [VIDEO]

comments.author: gaogao
comments.story: Super Mario Bros. has been released for the Commodore 64
comments.why: id's SMB3 PC port prototype that Nintendo declined
comments.text: The smooth scrolling is pretty hard. One of my favorite bits of Masters of Doom about id Software was when they hacked a port of Super Mario Bros 3 to the PC, but as history can tell, Nintendo didn't bite on that one. [VIDEO]
